name: Hungary
headline: Hungary: +0.5% growth in 2025, 4.4% inflation, debt 75% of GDP
sections: Hungary is a $247 billion economy (2025), the world's 56th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $50K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 15.1% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.4% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 14.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.4% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 14.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 75% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 79% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.7% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +1.7% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 141% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −28.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 88% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.7 years (2024). Population: 9.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
